title: RSE 1/12: Topocentric swe_calc support (swi_get_observer + TOPOCTR pipeline)
description:
### Summary
Implement `SEFLG_TOPOCTR` in the calc pipeline so `calc()` returns topocentric (observer-centred) positions instead of `Err(UnsupportedFlags)`. Port `swi_get_observer` (observer geocentric position+velocity in the equatorial-J2000/ICRS frame, derived from `config.topographic`) and subtract it inside the apparent-position functions. **This is the gating prerequisite for rise/set (RSE 3) and every eclipse `_where`/`_how`/`_loc` function** — all of them call `swe_calc(... | SEFLG_TOPOCTR)`.

**Architecture correction (do NOT follow the parent task's stale wording):** the port is STATELESS. There is no `swe_set_topo` global and no `swed.topd` cache. The observer is recomputed each call from `config.topographic: Option<TopoPosition>` (already present in `EphemerisConfig`, fields `longitude`/`latitude`/`altitude`). All methods stay `&self`.

### Files
- `src/topocentric.rs` (NEW) — `pub(crate) fn get_observer(jd_tt: f64, topo: &TopoPosition, config: &EphemerisConfig, models: &AstroModels) -> [f64; 6]` returning observer position+velocity in equatorial J2000.
- `src/lib.rs` — add `pub mod topocentric;` (alphabetical).
- `src/context.rs` — in `calc()` (line ~178) drop `TOPOCTR` from the `unsupported` mask; instead, if `flags.contains(TOPOCTR)` and `config.topographic.is_none()` return `Err(Error::CError("topocentric requires topographic position".into()))`. Compute `xobs` once and pass it down.
- `src/calc.rs` — thread the observer offset into `apparent_planet` (calc.rs:897), `apparent_sun` (1023), `apparent_moon` (1088). Add an `xobs: Option<[f64; 6]>` parameter to each (and to `calc_planet`/`calc_sun`/`calc_moon` callers), defaulting to `None` for the geocentric path.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_calc_topo.c`, `tests/golden-data/calc_topo.json`, `tests/golden/calc_topo.rs` (all NEW); add `mod calc_topo;` to `tests/golden/main.rs`.
- `docs/codebase-map.md` — add the `topocentric.rs` row + golden rows.

### Implementation steps
Read `docs/c-ref-topocentric.md` §1, §2, §3 (especially §3.1 and §3.2 — `SEFLG_NONUT` is always forced at these call sites, so implement ONLY the mean-frame path; the true-frame/backward-nutation branch is dead code from `calc()`'s perspective), §4, §5, §6, §7, §8 before coding.

1. **`get_observer`** (§3.2): from `topo` (geographic lon °, lat °, height m) build the observer's geocentric vector: geodetic→geocentric flattening using `EARTH_RADIUS`/`EARTH_OBLATENESS` (values in §3.2 / c-ref-eclipse-solar.md §0), local sidereal time via `crate::sidereal_time::sidereal_time0`, diurnal rotation velocity, then rotate the polar (lon/lat/r) form to cartesian with `math::polar_to_cartesian_with_speed`, and precess date→J2000 (`precession::precess`/`precess_speed`, direction `DateToJ2000`) with **no nutation** (NONUT forced). Follow the exact step order and helper list in §3.2 / §9. Match C's expression grouping (FP fidelity — see §3.2 hazard notes).
2. **Wire into `apparent_*`** (§4 plan, §5 moon, §6 sun): when `xobs` is `Some`, replace the geocentre with the observer — `xx[i] -= xobs[i]` for position and the aberration term `dx[i] -= (xobs[i] - xobs[i+3])` per §4. NOTE the asymmetry flagged in §6: the Sun path has **no** `xobs2` SPEED2 finite-difference term (planet/moon do). Moon and Sun do NOT call `deflect_light` (§7), so no topocentric deflection hookup there.
3. **`context.rs` `calc()`**: remove TOPOCTR from `unsupported`; add the `config.topographic.is_none()` guard; compute `xobs = Some(get_observer(...))` when TOPOCTR is set and pass through `calc_inner`→`calc_planet/sun/moon`.

### C reference
`docs/c-ref-topocentric.md` — §1 (concept), §2 (stateless note), §3.1–§3.2 (get_observer, mean-frame path only), §4/§5/§6 (application per body), §7 (deflection — informational), §8 (SPEED interaction). Constants also in `docs/c-ref-eclipse-solar.md` §0.

### Golden tests
- **C harness** `tests/c-gen/gen_calc_topo.c` (model on `tests/c-gen/gen_calc.c`): for each observer in `{(8.55,47.37,500), (-74.0,40.7,10), (139.7,35.7,40)}` call `swe_set_topo(lon,lat,alt)`, then for bodies `{SE_SUN, SE_MOON, SE_MERCURY, SE_MARS, SE_VENUS}` × epochs `{2451545.0, 2378496.5, 2469807.5}` call `swe_calc(jd, body, SEFLG_MOSEPH|SEFLG_TOPOCTR|SEFLG_EQUATORIAL|SEFLG_SPEED, xx, serr)`. Emit `{lon,lat,alt,body,jd,xx:[0..6]}`. Build: `cc -O2 -I../swisseph -o tests/c-gen/gen_calc_topo tests/c-gen/gen_calc_topo.c -L../swisseph -lswe -lm && ./tests/c-gen/gen_calc_topo > tests/golden-data/calc_topo.json`.
- **Rust test** `tests/golden/calc_topo.rs`: construct `Ephemeris` with `config.topographic = Some(TopoPosition{...})` per case, call `calc(jd, body, MOSEPH|TOPOCTR|EQUATORIAL|SPEED)`. Assert positions `assert_f64_eps(.., 1e-9)`, speeds `1e-7` (the documented stateless deflection-speed boundary applies — see CLAUDE.md `<stateless_tolerance>` §1; do NOT chase sub-mas speed deltas).
- `cargo test --test golden calc_topo -- --nocapture` passes.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden calc_topo -- --nocapture` passes (positions 1e-9, speeds 1e-7).
- Existing geocentric golden tests (`calc`) still pass (the `xobs: None` path must be behaviour-preserving).

### Escape hatch
If positions fail > 1e-8 after two debugging attempts, STOP and report failing cases (actual vs expected) + what you tried. For FP-fidelity mismatches read `sweph.c` `swi_get_observer` + the app_pos TOPOCTR branches directly (per CLAUDE.md §c_source_budget). Speed-only deltas near 1e-7 are the documented stateless boundary — accept, don't chase. Escalate to Opus after two attempts.

acceptance_criteria.text: cargo test --test golden calc_topo -- --nocapture passes (positions 1e-9, speeds 1e-7)
Existing geocentric golden tests (calc, calc_sweph, calc_jpl) still pass

execution_record: Ref doc's line-number pointers (calc.rs:897/1023/1088) covered only the generic apparent_planet/apparent_sun/apparent_moon (sweph/JPL backends). The golden test uses SEFLG_MOSEPH, which routes through the *separate* Moshier-specific calc_planet/calc_sun/calc_moon pipeline (compute_pipeline, heliocentric-only, no earth_bary/sun_bary concept) — that pipeline needed the identical xobs substitution applied independently since it doesn't share code with apparent_*. Threaded a new `config: &EphemerisConfig` parameter through calc_planet/calc_sun/calc_moon, apparent_planet/apparent_sun/apparent_moon, and their calc_*_jpl/calc_*_sweph wrappers so each can call the new topo_offset()/get_observer() at both the current and (for the planet/Moon paths) independently-recomputed retarded epoch, per c-ref-topocentric.md §4/§5's xobs2 pattern. All golden tests (existing + new calc_topo, 45 cases) and clippy passed on the first full run — no debugging iteration needed.

messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention (medium).

Finding: Topocentric golden coverage only exercises the MOSEPH SPEED3 path (tests/golden/calc_topo.rs:60-62). The test hardcodes MOSEPH|TOPOCTR|EQUATORIAL|SPEED, which forces SPEED3 and validates the Moshier 3-point position path — but the generic apparent_planet/apparent_sun/apparent_moon xobs wiring shared by the SWIEPH/JPL backends is never exercised against C golden data, nor are non-SPEED3 flag shapes (e.g. TOPOCTR|SPEED|NOABERR, TRUEPOS). A regression in the generic-path xobs wiring could ship silently.

Recommendation: extend the golden matrix with C-generated SWIEPH/JPL topocentric cases and at least one non-SPEED3 flag shape (TOPOCTR|SPEED|NOABERR) for Sun, Moon, and a planet, before treating TOPOCTR as verified across the full calc pipeline.

Codex independently re-ran cargo build/clippy/golden tests (calc_topo, calc, calc_sweph, calc_jpl) — all passed; the acceptance-criteria claims check out for what they cover, but coverage itself is narrower than the task implies ("Existing geocentric golden tests still pass" doesn't establish topocentric correctness on the sweph/JPL path).
